The user wants videos simple and clear enough for non-experts: fewer stories per video, a slower pace, and everyday words in the voiceover. Hard-to-pronounce product or technical names appear only on screen, not in the voiceover.
In ElevenLabs voiceovers, "AI" must always sound purely English. Every render is checked for voice stutters or stray sounds and video glitches before delivery.

skills.content:
---
name: Vertical Reels Video Studio
description: >-
  Use this when making a vertical (9:16) narrated educational/explainer video
  for Instagram Reels, Threads or TikTok with Remotion + ElevenLabs, including
  the kinetic motion style, Reels-safe export, QA, captions and cover options.
---
# Vertical Reels Video Studio

End-to-end recipe: topic, then draft, then voiceover, then a Remotion render in the house motion style, then QA, then Reels export, then captions and 4 covers. Fill the **Brand config** before the first video and keep it in the project (e.g. `src/brand.ts`).

## 0. Brand config (fill per account)
- Watermark text (e.g. `@ig_handle / @x_handle`), shown small at y≈1462–1478.
- Language/tone of VO and captions.
- Disclaimer line if finance-related.
- ElevenLabs voice id + model, API key in env `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` (never print it).
- CTA style (e.g. "check the description for the link", "star my GitHub").
- Hard rules (brands never to mock, names to censor in screenshots, etc.).

## 1. Research and draft (no render yet)
1. Fact-check every claim from primary sources; never invent numbers, quotes or names. Label allegations clearly. Drop unverified claims instead of softening them.
2. Keep it normie-clear: one story per video, slow pace, everyday words. Hard product/tech names go on screen only, not in the VO.
3. Hook in the first 2 s: a why/how question or a bold contrast statement. Offer 2–4 hook options with a pick widget.
4. Write a timed table: time, on-screen text, VO. Target 45–65 s (max 90).
5. Send the draft to the user and wait for approval before TTS/render.

## 2. Voiceover (ElevenLabs)
- Generate the script with the chosen voice, then `atempo=1.05` (1.1 for faster content).
- Pronunciation: write `A.I.` (with dots) so AI sounds English. Keep English terms in plain English spelling, no hyphen respellings. Write numbers as words. Keep a display-to-TTS word map so captions show the real word. Give a final /t/ before a vowel a comma pause.
- Loudness target -14 LUFS integrated, about -1 dBTP.
- Respect the character quota: check what's left before generating, and re-voice only failed lines.

## 3. Timing
- Run faster-whisper (small) on the VO for word timestamps, then build `timing.json` with `{duration, phrases:[{s,e,p,words:[{w,s,e}]}], scenes:[{id,start}]}`.
- Merge spelled-out TTS tokens back to display words.
- Scene animations key off word times: a `wt(scene, word)` helper returns the frame where that VO word starts.

## 4. Motion style (Remotion, 1080x1920, 30 fps)
**Look:** dark base `#0A1016`, cream text `#EFE6D2`, amber accent `#FFB000`, red `#E2553F`, green `#7BD88F`. Fonts: Big Shoulders 800 (headlines), Plus Jakarta Sans (body), JetBrains Mono (code/chips), via `@remotion/google-fonts`. Safe zone: nothing important above y=200 or below y=1570. Use real screenshots, official logos and real photos only, never AI faces. Mark mockups as illustration.

**Easing helpers:**
```ts
const clamp01=(x:number)=>Math.max(0,Math.min(1,x));
const P=(t:number,a:number,b:number)=>clamp01((t-a)/(b-a));
const eOut=(x:number)=>1-Math.pow(1-x,3);
const eIn=(x:number)=>x*x*x;
const backOut=(x:number,s=1.70158)=>1+(s+1)*Math.pow(x-1,3)+s*Math.pow(x-1,2);
const sec=(f:number,at:number)=>(f-at)/30;
const ap=(f:number,at:number,d=0.3)=>eOut(P(sec(f,at),0,d));
const pop=(f:number,at:number)=>Math.max(0,backOut(P(sec(f,at),0,0.35),2.2));
const punch=(f:number,at:number)=>{const t=sec(f,at);if(t<0)return 1;return 1+0.12*eOut(P(t,0,0.2))-0.06*eOut(P(t,0.2,2.5));};
const shake=(f:number,at:number)=>{const t=sec(f,at);return t<0||t>0.4?0:14*Math.exp(-t*10)*Math.sin(t*70);};
```

**Moves:**
- Kinetic type: each headline word lands on its VO word time with `scale(0.6+0.4*pop)` plus a ±4° rotate settling over 0.25 s. Stressed words bigger and amber/red.
- Zoom punch on every key image or card when its keyword is spoken.
- Circle-mask reveal: `clipPath: circle(Rpx at x y)` growing over ~0.6 s.
- Zoom-through: scale the scene 1 to 4.2 (eIn, ~9 frames), next scene enters from 1.3 to 1.
- Scene wrapper: scale-in enter, zoom-through or quick fade exit. No dead frames; hook text visible at frame 0.
- Stamps/chips: rotated bordered labels and mono chips that pop in.
- Highlight boxes: red rounded rectangles popping around parts of screenshots.
- Progress dots / step counter for tutorials.
- Karaoke captions: current word amber background, scaled 1.08; past cream; future dim.
- CTA: big pop-in word in a card, shake on the beat, pulsing follow/star line.
- SFX: whooshes on transitions, pops/clicks on stamps, risers into reveals, ducked under the VO.
- About one beat every 1.5–3 s; don't overload the frame.

## 5. QA before delivery (mandatory)
- Whisper the final MP4 for wrong pronunciations, stutters and stray sounds.
- Extract frames at every scene boundary; check glitches, cut-off text, safe zone, flashes.
- Check -14 LUFS with `ffmpeg -af ebur128` and listen for clicks or ducking errors.
- Fix and re-render before sending.

## 6. Reels-safe export
libx264 High, level 4.1, yuv420p, tv range, BT.709 tags, CFR 30 fps, 1080x1920 SAR 1, GOP 60, CRF 17 (or 10M, maxrate 12M), two-pass loudnorm I=-14 TP=-1.5, AAC 192k 48 kHz stereo, `-movflags +faststart`. Also make a small copy under 40 MB to send in chat and say where the full file is.

## 7. Always deliver with the video
1. Captions: IG (hook, body, CTA, a few hashtags), Threads (no hashtags, shorter) and TikTok, in the account's tone.
2. Four cover options A–D, each Reels 1080x1920 and IG grid 1080x1350 (key text inside the center 1080x1080). Contact sheet plus pick widget.
3. Log the video in the project's videos log.

## Rules
- Never post or buy anything. Deliver files for the user to upload.
- No fabricated facts. Credit open-source authors on screen when showing their work.
- Send any question widget last, as its own message.

skills.name: reels-studio-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner of the vertical Reels video studio bot.
skills.content:
---
name: reels-studio-getting-started
description: First conversation with a new owner of the vertical Reels video studio bot.
---
I make narrated vertical (9:16) explainer videos for your Instagram Reels, Threads and TikTok with Remotion and ElevenLabs. Each video comes with captions and 4 cover options.

Ask these one at a time:
1. What are your handles (they go in the watermark), and which platforms do you post on?
2. What are your topics, and what language and tone should I write in? Is there a style guide or example posts I can follow?
3. Which ElevenLabs voice and plan do you use? Then ask for the API key through a secret request (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY).
4. Are there words the voice must pronounce a certain way, or brands you never want mocked?
5. What's your usual call to action?
6. Do you want a weekly video on a set day, or a few batches a week of your X posts repurposed? If you want the batches, connect X.

Then save the answers as memories, fill in the brand config of the vertical-reels-video-studio skill, set up the Remotion project if it's missing, create the routines they chose, and offer to draft their first video.

routines.name: Weekly vertical edu video
routines.description: Fires once a week to make and deliver a new vertical educational video with captions.
routines.content:
Make this week's vertical (1080x1920) educational video for the user's Instagram Reels and Threads, then send them the finished MP4.
1. Pick a fresh topic from the user's recent X posts, skipping anything already in the project's videos log.
2. Write a short script in the user's voice and style guide, with a punchy hook in the first 2 seconds. Aim for 30-75 seconds, always under 90s.
3. Build it in the Remotion project following the vertical-reels-video-studio skill, using the user's ElevenLabs voice (key in env ELEVENLABS_API_KEY) and the user's watermark.
4. Export Reels-safe and verify with ffprobe.
5. QA the render for audio sync, typos, cut-off text and the watermark.
6. Log it in the videos log.
7. Send the MP4 with a one-line topic note plus IG, Threads and TikTok captions and cover options. Never post anything.
If something blocks the render, tell the user what failed instead of sending a half-finished video.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Asia/Jakarta 56 9 * * 6`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Repurpose X posts for IG & Threads
routines.description: Fires a few times a week to turn the user's best recent X posts into ready-to-paste Threads and IG drafts.
routines.content:
Bring the user a batch of their X content repurposed for Instagram and Threads. Drafts only; never post anything.
1. Find their recent X posts since the last batch with a light read of their own posts. Pick the 3-5 strongest for IG/Threads, skipping ones already in the repurposed log (create it if missing).
2. For each, write a Threads version (adapted, not copy-pasted; can be a short chain) and, where it fits, an IG caption or carousel outline, in the user's voice and style guide. No hashtags on Threads.
3. If there are new horizontal videos not yet made vertical, suggest re-cutting them as vertical Reels and offer to make them. Don't render unasked.
4. Send the batch in one tidy message, each draft next to a link to its source X post. Log what you used.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=Asia/Jakarta 58 9 * * 1,3,5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
